title: 6th National Pharmacovigilance Week 2026 Inaugural Ceremony
bodyHtml:
🔹 6th National Pharmacovigilance Week 2026: 17th -23rd September 2026🔹
The theme; “Promoting Rational Use of Medicines through Pharmacovigilance - A Step Towards
Safer Healthcare” of this year's National Pharmacovigilance Week highlights an essential connection:
rational use of medicines and pharmacovigilance are closely linked to medication safety and
better patient outcomes.
Inaugural Ceremony of 6th National Pharmacovigilance Week (NPW) 2026, was organised by the
National Coordination Centre - Pharmacovigilance Programme of India (NCC–PvPI), Indian
Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India at
Padmashri Nitya Anand Auditorium Hall, ALRC Building, IPC on 17th September, 2026
The programme brought together perspectives from pharmacovigilance, clinical practice, public
health, regulation and patient safety.
The inaugural session included:
∙Welcome Address by Dr. Jai Prakash, Officer-in-Charge, PvPI
∙Opening Remarks by Dr. V. Kalaiselvan, Secretary-cum-Scientific Director, IPC
∙Virtual remarks by Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Director General, ICMR
∙Remarks by Shri Aditya Kumar Mamgain, Deputy Secretary, MoHFW, Govt. of India
∙Remarks from Prof. Sangeeta Sharma and Dr. Abdul Nasser experts representing clinical
practice, public health and the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare
∙Video messages from Shri Tukaram Mundhe, Commissioner FDA, Maharashtra, and Dr.
Shanthi Pal, Team Lead, Pharmacovigilance, WHO
Release of PvPI Resource Material:
Newsletter Volume 16 Issue 2, 2026
The technical sessions were particularly relevant to the theme:
“Pharmacovigilance and Rational Use of Medicines: Two Pillars of Medication Safety”​
- Prof. Sangeeta Sharma, IHBAS, New Delhi
“Beyond Medicines: Role of MvPI in Strengthening Patient Safety”​
- Dr. Abdul Nasser, Max Hospital, Vaishali
Pharmacovigilance is not simply about reporting adverse drug reactions-it is about continuously
learning from medicine use, identifying potential risks, generating safety information and using that
knowledge to support safer healthcare practices.
The inclusion of Materiovigilance Programme of India (MvPI) also emphasised the broader vision of
patient safety, extending beyond medicines to medical devices.
✨ Key takeaway
​
Every ADR report, every safety signal evaluated, and every effort towards rational medicine use
contributes to building a stronger culture of patient safety.
A meaningful beginning to #NPW2026 and an opportunity to reaffirm our collective responsibility
towards safer medicines and safer healthcare.
